channel.title: Yasmin's Blog
channel.description: Yasmin's Blog is an independent New York journal about food, neighborhood institutions, culture and street photography.

item.title: Turkish Immigrant Restaurant Owners in New York & London
item.description: How Turkish immigrant families built restaurant communities in New York and London, from ocakbaşı grills to bakeries, often to fund their children's future.

item.title: 4 Photos from Salerno: Light, Lemons and the Amalfi Coast
item.description: A four-frame photo essay from Salerno, the port city at the edge of Italy's Amalfi Coast: lemon stalls, the lungomare promenade, steep alleys and evening light.

item.title: 4 Photos from Economy Candy, NYC's Classic Candy Store
item.description: Inside Economy Candy, the Lower East Side candy store on Rivington Street selling old-fashioned sweets since 1937. A four-photo essay plus a visitor's guide.

item.title: 24 Hours in New Orleans: A Mini Mardi Gras Bender
item.description: How to spend 24 hours in New Orleans during Carnival season: beignets, parades, the St. Charles streetcar, king cake and live music on Frenchmen Street.

item.title: Photoville and "This Is 18", a New York Times Zine
item.description: The New York Times' "This Is 18" project showed life for 18-year-old girls worldwide, photographed by women. Why it resonated at Photoville.

item.title: On Pole Dancing: Strength, Artistry and Community in NYC
item.description: Pole dancing has moved from the club to the studio and the competition stage. NYC pole fitness: its history, the strength it takes and how to start.

item.title: Stick and Poke Tattoos: Inside the Hand-Poke Revival
item.description: Stick and poke tattoos moved from DIY to fine-art studios in NYC and Tokyo. What hand-poking is, how it differs from machine work and how to find an artist.

item.title: Pies 'n' Thighs Brunch: Brooklyn Fried Chicken & Biscuits
item.description: Pies 'n' Thighs in Williamsburg serves Southern comfort food: fried chicken, biscuits, donuts and pie. What to order for brunch and how to plan your visit.

item.title: Defining Your Own Rules: The New Age of Spirituality
item.description: Tarot, crystals, witchcraft and shops like Catland Books in Brooklyn: how a generation builds a DIY spirituality, plus what eggshells mean in witchcraft.

item.title: Dollar Pizza on the Lower East Side: More Than a Slice
item.description: The cheap slice is a New York institution. A guide to dollar pizza on the Lower East Side: its history, why prices crept up and where to get a late-night slice.

item.title: Porto Rico Importing Co.: NYC Coffee Shop Since 1907
item.description: Porto Rico Importing Co. has sold coffee and tea on Bleecker Street since 1907. A guide to the NYC coffee shop: what to buy, the bean bins and wholesale coffee.

item.title: Ramen Quotes, Notes and Details from a NYC Ramen Festival
item.description: What reporting on a New York ramen festival teaches about food journalism: how to take notes, gather quotes and catch details. Plus our favorite ramen quotes.

item.title: Subway Photos, Trial No. 1: Learning from Walker Evans
item.description: New York subway portraits inspired by Walker Evans' hidden-camera subway photography of 1938 to 1941, with notes on candid street photography and ethics.

item.title: Little Tong Noodle Shop: Yunnan Mixian Comes to New York
item.description: Little Tong Noodle Shop brought Yunnan mixian rice noodles to New York. The story of chef Simone Tong's East Village restaurant and what made it special.

item.title: Mountain Province Coffee: Filipino Beans in Williamsburg
item.description: Mountain Province Espresso Bar in East Williamsburg served single-origin coffee from the Philippine highlands, plus Filipino baked goods. A Brooklyn café story.

item.title: Katz's Deli Pastrami: Why It's So Expensive & What to Order
item.description: A guide to Katz's Delicatessen on the Lower East Side: how the ticket system works, what to order, why the pastrami costs so much and if cats can eat it.
